docs.title: What is MysterSmith?
docs.text: My name is Benke Smith, I'm a magic app developer from Hungary, and the creator of the "Smith" apps. The initial idea of MysterSmith was born in May 2023. As the PeekSmith app was evolving, I’ve added many features that were already beyond the app’s initial purpose (to be a companion app for the PeekSmith devices). I believed it was time for a brand new app that can offer everything the PeekSmith app does, and many-many more (including proper routine management, unique routines, and a much wider support of magic hardware). I’ve always planned to introduce a subscription system at some point, and MysterSmith seemed to be the right  tool for this.

docs.title: What can you do with MysterSmith? Click here to discover...
Free features for everyone?? Click here to read on...
docs.text:
In February 2025 the MysterSmith app started as an evolved version of the PeekSmith app, which means it offered all the features that the PeekSmith app had(except firmware updates for Electricks hardware), and all add-ons purchased for the PeekSmith app continued working in MysterSmith the same way. Since then I've added new features and routines gradually, based on user requests and priorities. However, you will still need the PeekSmith app for firmware updates, even if you "switch" to MysterSmith. Also some exclusive features (like advanced Atom 2 functions) are only added to the PeekSmith app, which is now maintained by Electricks.

While most of the new features/routines will also be available as a one-time purchase, the subscription models will offer many-many more, especially for those who perform regularly. While the BASIC plan will be more than enough for most hobby-magicians, there is also a PREMIUM plan available (limited to 50 users!!!), intended for professional magicians.

docs.title: What can you do with the API?
docs.text: You can use the "Recognized text API" in 3rd party apps to retrieve the last recognized text by the PeekSmith app. The API can also return the last recognized time by the TimeSmith app.

docs.title: The prerequisites of using the API
docs.text:
To use the API for retrieving the last recognized text by the PeekSmith app, you have to purchase the API access add-on (click here for more info). To retrieve the last recognized time by the TimeSmith app, you don't need to buy additional add-ons.

IMPORTANT: If you already purchased the Multi-Display add-on earlier, then you already have the API access feature, no need to buy it again!

docs.title: The secret token
docs.text: You will need a secret token from either the PeekSmith or the TimeSmith app, which you can find under your Username and PIN (in USER SETTINGS). You can re-generate (refresh) your token at any time, in case you want to share it only temporarily.

docs.title: The API URL
docs.text:
To get the last recognized text from the PeekSmith app (or the last recognized time from the TimeSmith app) in simple text format, you'll have to use the following API URL (enter your own secret token from the PeekSmith or TimeSmith app instead of ABC1234DEF):

https://bsmagic.app/api/get_rectext.php?token=ABC1234DEF

docs.title: Advanced API URL
docs.text:
To get the result in a JSON format, add this to the end of the above URLs (after your secret token):

&json=1

The response will have this format:

{"found":1,"id":"23","text":"Testing 123"}

found: 1 if a recognized text was found, 0 if not found id: the ID of the database record (it will increase with every new text reconition) text: the recognized text (or time)

docs.title: What can I do with MysterSmith?
What can I do with MysterSmith?
docs.text:
The MysterSmith app has 3 main features:

  • Receive information
  • Transform data / generate new content
  • Send information

docs.title: Receiving information
docs.text:
MysterSmith can receive information from different sources:

Bluetooth devices:

  • impression boards
  • NFC readers
  • BT remotes
  • PeekSmith 3 (buttons, motion, magnet detector)
  • other devices (like Labco Scrabble)

Other apps:

  • data sent via the custom URL scheme (mystersmith://?text=xxxx)
  • data received from WEB APIs (WEB-polling from any source)
  • local HTTP requests (http://localhost:62369/data?text=xxxxx)

Other WEB sources:

  • text from any WEB browser (WEB-input)
  • drawings, handwritings using the WEB-doodle

Manual input in the app (by an assistant):

  • impromptu text (or predefined texts)
  • playing cards
  • colors
  • drawings

The Advanced Input Methods add-on offers inputs like:

  • fake passcode screen
  • swipe screen (for numbers)
  • more Bluetooth remotes
  • voice recognition (coming soon!!!)
  • Bluetooth dice (coming soon!!!)
  • fake calculator input (coming soon!!!)

...and possibly some more.

The received data (text or image) is stored in the text/image buffer in the app, and also in the cloud (for API access).

docs.title: Transforming data, generating new content
docs.text:
You can work with any text or image that is stored in the text/image buffer. At the moment the app offers these options:

  • recognize handwritten text/numbers, celebrity names, timestamps, ESP signs, playing cards
  • correct misspellings and typos in recognized handwrittemn texts
  • analyze drawings and turn them into keywords or longer descriptions
  • turn numbers to an ESP symbol or a smiley, or generate a magic square
  • turn any 3-4 digit number into Pi Revelations numbers
  • display the dictionary location of any English word (using the Dictionary API add-on)
  • re-order recognized numbers into a list of LOTTO numbers
  • using the custom A.I. prompt, you can turn any recognized text/drawing into anything
  • create sharpie drawings from text, drawings or images (received from other apps)
  • "outsource" the tranformation process to other apps, like Bridge (send data, and receive the result)

Soon I will introduce the Transformer add-on, which will offer a lot more options for transforming text, drawings and images.

docs.title: Sending information
docs.text:
Finally, when you have a text or image prepared, you can send it to various devices and 3rd party apps.

You can peek text, images and drawings on:

  • PeekSmith 3 device
  • Electricks Bond watch
  • Super Sharpie
  • Sharpeek marker
  • Apple watch
  • WearOS watch
  • any smartwatch (using notifications)
  • the WEB-screen (in any WEB-browser)

...with support coming soon for:

  • MrCard
  • Iarvel credit card
  • Spectra
  • Lumen Eye

You can hear recognized text or thedescription of a recognized drawing, photo through a secret earpiece.

You can displaypredicted text (printed or handwritten), drawings, photos, magic squares, clock predictions etc. on e-ink devices, like:

  • Teleport
  • Pitata Inversion Board (chalkboard)
  • Pitata Prediction Keychain
  • Reinkstone iPhone cases

...with support coming soon for:

  • Lumen Prism

You can printpredictions of text, drawings, photos, magic squares, clock predictions etc. on printers, like:

  • Glyphs / Peripage
  • Cosmos / L2
  • Pitata Printer
  • Cat printers

...with support coming soon for COLOR printers, like:

  • HP Sprocket (1st edition)
  • HP Sprocket Plus
  • Polaroid ZIP
  • Polaroid Mint

You can send text and images to:

  • any 3rd party app, using custom URL schemes
  • any WEB API

docs.title: What can you do with the FREE app?
(without purchasing add-ons or a subscription)
docs.text:
Good news: many features in MysterSmith are FREE for everyone!!! :-)

DISPLAYING DATA:

  • you can display received text on the BLACK SCREEN
  • you can display handwritings, signatures, playing cards, magic squares, Tic-Tac-Toe boards etc. on the Doodle screen
  • you can display text, drawing and images on the PeekSmith 3 and Bond devices (no add-on required until the end of 2025)
  • you can display text on the SB Watch 2 (no add-on required until the end of 2025)
  • you can display images, handwritings, playing cards, magic squares, ESP symbols etc. on Teleport (no add-on required until the end of 2025)
  • you can display text and drawings on the MrCard device (no add-on required until the end of 2025)

RECEIVING DATA:

  • WEB-polling: you can receive info from any WEB API (like Inject, WikiTest, Elips, Topix, Goo etc. or any other source)
  • Custom URL scheme: you can receive data from any app through the mystersmith:// scheme
  • HTTP Socket: you can receive data from any app or WEB-browser (on the same local WiFi network) on localhost:62369
  • WEB-input (WEB-thumper): you can receive data from any WEB-browser, from anywhere in the world (planet Earth)
  • manual input: your assistant can enter text/numbers, playing cards, colors etc. manually
  • you can use the built-in NFC reader of your phone to receive data
  • you can use supported NFC readers to receive data
  • on Android you can catch and display notifications from any 3rd party app
  • you can view words (and point values) from the Scrabble device by Labco
  • you can display numbers coming from the Quantum calculator

IMPRESSION BOARDS:

  • you can display handwriting and drawings from impression boards on the Doodle screen and on the BLACK SCREEN

HANDWRITING RECOGNITION:

  • you get 250 free recognition credits, to be used with the Google Vision recognition engine (one recognition = 1 credit)

CONTROLLING THE APP:

  • you can use Volume buttons (and bluetooth shutter remotes that simulate a volume button press) to trigger any available action in the app
  • you can tap the corners on impression board devices to trigger any available action in the app
  • you can use the buttons of the PeekSmith 3 and Bond devices to trigger any available action in the app (no add-on required until the end of 2025)
  • you can use the buttons of the Quantum calculator to trigger some actions in the app (no add-on required until the end of 2025)

TESTING E-INK DEVICES AND PRINTERS:

  • you can connect any supported e-ink device and printer, and send a TEST image/text to see if they work properly with the app

docs.title: The WearOS watch app
docs.text:
If you use the APK versions of my apps, you will need to delete and reinstall all the WearOS watch companion apps. This is a step by step guide that will help you installing the WearOS watch companion apps, using a Windows PC.

You can jump to the end of the page to watch the tutorial video before you begin the installation process.

docs.title: Enable developer mode on the watch
docs.text:
The first thing you should do is to enable developer mode on your watch. (If developer mode is already enabled, you can skip to the next chapter.)

  • open Settings
  • go to "About watch"
  • tap "Software information"
  • quickly tap "Software version" 5 times in a row
  • developer mode should now be enabled

docs.title: Download my WearOS installer app for Windows
docs.text:
You should download my WearOS installer app for Windows from the following URL: bsmagic.app/apps/wearos/WearOS_watch_installer_v1.2.exe

After downloading the EXE file, you can place it in a new, dedicated folder (like "WearOS installer").

docs.title: Prepare the watch for the connection
docs.text:
Please follow these steps to prepare your watch for connecting wirelessly with your PC:

  • open Settings
  • scroll down, and select "Developer options"
  • find "ADB debugging" and enable it
  • find "Wireless debugging" and enable it
  • scroll down until you see the IP address and Port number of the watch
  • write down the IP address and the Port number (example: 192.168.1.37 is the IP address and 34107 is the Port number)
  • scroll down and tap "+ Pair new device"
  • write down the Pairing codeand the Port number(the IP address should be the same, but the Port number is different)
  • proceed with the next steps without exiting this screen

docs.title: Use the Windows WearOS Installer to install the watch apps
docs.text:
Now it's time to run the WearOS_watch_installer_v1.2.exe file, and perform the installation of the companion apps...

  • delete all my magic WearOS apps from your watch, that were installed before from Google Play
  • make sure your watch is on the same local (WiFi) network as your PC
  • on your PC double-click the file "WearOS_watch_installer_v1.2.exe"
  • follow the instructions of the tutorial video
  • when everything is OK and the watch apps are installed, you can close the installer app

docs.title: F.A.Q. - read before you ask
docs.text:
- What can I do with MysterSmith?

  • You can receive data (from devices or other apps), you can process/transform that information or generate new data, and finally you can send the result to various devices or any other app. Click here to explore the possibilities...

- Does the basic app have FREE features?

  • Good news: many features in MysterSmith are FREE for everyone!!! :-) You can receive data from many sources, display the data on some screens/devices, and you also get some free text recognition credits. Click here to discover all the FREE features...

- Is MysterSmith a subscription-only app? Do I need to subscribe to use it?

  • No, no, ABSOLUTELY NOT!!! You can install and use MysterSmith as if it were the PeekSmith app. You can use every feature, every add-on that you already used in the PeekSmith app (except for some features added in the PeekSmith app after March 2025) - and you will get lots of new FREE features and functions as well!!! There are new add-ons that you can buy separately if you need them, or you CAN subscribe if you'd like to get access to all current and future features and add-ons. But if you don't need the new paid features, you can continue using MysterSmith instead of the PeekSmith app totally FREE.

- How can I install MysterSmith? I don't see it in the AppStore or Google Play...

  • MysterSmith is an underground app, not available for the general public. You can install it from TestFlight on iOS, and install an APK version on Android. For the detailed download information please click here.

- Can I use MysterSmith the same way I used the PeekSmith app, without subscribing or paying more?

  • Yes! MysterSmith basically started as a PeekSmith app "clone", and you can continue using every feature, every purchased add-on the same way. Some features (like advanced Atom 2 functions) that were added to the PeekSmith app after March 2025, might be only available in the PeekSmith app. In MysterSmith you will also get some new features for free. However, some new routines and premium features that will be added later, will require either a subscription or a one-time purchase.

- Can I continue using the PeekSmith app? Will it be updated regularly?

  • Sure! The PeekSmith app won't be abandoned, there will be updates, and support for new Electricks hardware will be added. In fact you will still need the PeekSmith app for firmware updates, even if you "switch" to MysterSmith. Also some exclusive features (like advanced Atom 2 functions) will be only added to the PeekSmith app, which is now maintained by Electricks. You can go ahead and use both apps at the same time.

- Can I use MysterSmith on both Android and iOS?

  • Yes! Like all my apps, MysterSmith will be available for both platforms. On Android I will distribute the app as an APK installer, and on iOS you will be able to get it on TestFlight (later I will publish it to the AppStore as an Unlisted app, so no outsiders will find it).

- If I switch to MysterSmith, and would like to use the new features/routines, will I have to subscribe?

  • No, there will be one-time purchase options for every new feature and routine. Subscriptions will give you a lot more benefits though (please read the corresponding pages as well).

- If I subscribe, will I access all functions/routines in the app, or there could be some additional fees?

  • All subscribers will have access to all functions/features and routines in the app. However, there could be some special routines - like A.I. video avatar predictions - which would require a usage-based credit system (using 3rd party paid services through my service). PREMIUM subscribers will get some free credits, and a 50% discount of all credit packages. As a bonus, Google text recognition credits will be FREE for all subscribers!

- How can I subscribe to MysterSmith?

  • Please sign in to the Account Manager with the same account as you use on your phone to sign in to the MysterSmith app.

docs.title: Get the Bridge A.I. app
docs.text:
Bridge A.I. is an iOS app by Marc Kerstein. Get the app from the AppStore:

apps.apple.com/us/app/bridge-magic-app-ai/id6739980516

docs.title: API & A.I. Access add-on needed
docs.text:
You will need to have the API & A.I. Access add-on for sending data to Bridge. You can either purchase the add-on separately, or subscribe for MysterSmith (which will give you access to all available add-ons). You can purchase the add-on here:

bsmagic.app/payment/index.php?item=sendtoapi

docs.title: Copy/paste your Bridge URL
docs.text:
• open the Bridge app
  • tap on Input
  • select "Input API"
  • tap on "Copy API URL" To Clipboard

(the same API URL is used to send data from Bridge to MysterSmith)

  • open MysterSmith
  • go to Settings, and scroll down to API + A.I. ACCESS ADD-ON
  • find "Your Bridge URL" and paste your URL
  • alternatively (if you only want to receive data), go to WEB-POLLING, edit WEB data sources, enable Bridge A.I. and paste your API URL

docs.title: Receive data from Bridge
docs.text:
• you don't need to open/run the Bridge app on your iPhone
  • go to Settings, WEB-POLLING, edit WEB data sources, enable Bridge A.I. and make sure your API URL is entered
  • start WEB-polling
  • you will start receiving new data from Bridge

docs.title: Send data to Bridge
docs.text:
• you don't need to open/run the Bridge app on your iPhone
  • make sure you have the API & A.I. Access add-on (purchased separately, or subscribed)
  • you can invoke the action "last text to Bridge" by any trigger available (PS3 button, volume button, Atom 2 remote, Apple watch tap/swipe, or even automatically after recognizing a text)
  • or you can go to API + A.I. ACCESS ADD-ON, "Send text to WEB API" -> "Manage", and enter "bridge" (or "!bridge" to send text automatically)

docs.title: Full routine idea
docs.text:
Your spectator writes the name of a celebrity on an impression board, and you peek the birthday of the celebrity on your PeekSmith 3.

  • in the Bridge app select the A.I. transform action "Birthday of this celebrity"
  • for both input and output select the API
  • you can now close the Bridge app
  • connect your PeekSmith 3 in MysterSmith
  • connect your impression board in MysterSmith
  • in TEXT RECOGNITION settings set these values:
  • Trigger when idle: 5 sec (you can adjust this as you like)
  • Action after recognized: 1 sec
  • Trigger action: last text to Bridge
  • under WEB-POLLING make sure Bridge is enabled as a source (you can disable other sources)
  • go to the main performance screen
  • start WEB-polling
  • start the Doodle or BLACK screen
  • the spectator can write the name of a celebrity
  • after the text is recogniued, the name is being sent to Bridge
  • Bridge gets the birthday of the celebrity using A.I.
  • MysterSmith receives the birthday via WEB-polling
  • the birthday is displayed on the PeekSmith 3

docs.title: The routine
docs.text: You open a (fake) Google search page on the spectator's phone, and pretend to search for something (place, object, country, people etc.), then place the phone face down on a table. You give a spectator an impression board, and they write something on it. When they are ready, after a few seconds they can turn over their phone, and they will freak out that you have searched for the same thing they wrote!!!

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Basically you have to do a text recognition from an impression board (or the in-app Doodle screen, or using the WEB-doodle on another spectator's phone), and the app will send the recognized text to your Inject account's fake Google search page (use https://qq1.us/username). Alternatively you can use other text input methods, like manual text entry in the MysterSmith app, reading an NFC card, polling a WEB API source or using the WEB-thumper from any browser, and send that text to Inject.

If you go with text recognition, please read all info on this page: Text recognition

docs.title: API & A.I. Access add-on needed
docs.text:
To be able to send data from the MysterSmith app to 3rd party apps and APIs, you have to buy the "API & A.I. Access" add-on. Alternatively you can subscribe to MysterSmith, and get access to all the available add-ons.

More information: "API & A.I. Access" add-on

docs.title: Inject account setup
docs.text: First of all you have to buy Inject 2.0 by Greg Rostami, and set up a username. Then in the MysterSmith app go to Settings, and scroll down to the API + A.I. ACCESS section. There you can enter your Inject ID / username. The Inject account number should be automatically filled in (in some cases it's not the same as the Inject ID). In case the account number is not properly set automatically, you can manually enter it (ask for help from someone who knows how to get the account number).

docs.title: Send text to Inject (manually)
docs.text:
The easiest and best way to send data to Inject is to manually trigger the "last text to Inject" action. You can select a trigger in the ACTION CONTROL section of the Settings (or at any other section where you can set actions). A trigger can be any of the following actions:

  • volume button press
  • PeekSmith 3 button press
  • PeekSmith 3 magnet sensor
  • PeekSmith 3 tap
  • Atom remote button short/long press
  • Apple watch tap/swipe
  • WearOS watch tap/swipe
  • ...and many-many more (please explore the settings)

As soon as you trigger the "last text to Inject" action (in the "Text buffer" section of the actions list), the fake Google page will receive the text and perform the real Google search.

docs.title: Second method: send to active APIs (manually)
docs.text:
With this method you can send the text not only to Inject, but to any other active WEB API URLs as well. To add Inject as an API URL, you have to go to API + A.I. ACCESS ACCESS and select "Send text to WEB API" - "Manage". In a new empty field enter "inject" (see the screenshot below), and make sure the toggle is activated. You can add other URLs as well, and activate them with the toggle.

When you trigger the action "last text to WEB APIs" then all active URLs will receive the text. I recommend using this method only if you need to send the text to other targets as well, and not only to Inject.

docs.title: Third method: send to active APIs (automatically)
docs.text:
This method is almost the same as the previous one, except this time you add a ! mark before "inject" when you enter the API URL. If you enter "!inject" then the recognized text (or the data from other sources) will be sent to Inject automatically, without using any action trigger.

This method can be dangerous, because you might accidentally send data to Inject. I recommend using the previous methods, unless you need to send data to Inject automatically, without any interaction (action trigger). Of course all other active API URLs that start with a ! mark will also receive the data.

docs.title: API & A.I. Access add-on needed
docs.text:
You will need to have the API & A.I. Access add-on for both sending and receiving data through Notarized. You can either purchase the add-on separately, or subscribe for MysterSmith (which will give you access to all available add-ons). You can purchase the add-on here:

bsmagic.app/payment/index.php?item=sendtoapi

docs.title: Get your MysterSmith token
docs.text:
• open MysterSmith
  • go to Settings - USER SETTINGS
  • tap your username
  • copy the secret token (grey icon)

docs.title: Set up Notarized on your iPhone
docs.text:
• open Notarized
  • tap Settings
  • scroll down to API FUNCTIONALITY
  • enable API Functions
  • for the API URL, enter this: https://bsmagic.app/api/notarized/TOKEN (replace TOKEN with your token from MysterSmith)
  • leave the API Key empty
  • API Action:
  • select "Send to API" if you want to send text from Notarized (fake Notes app on spectator's phone) to MysterSmith
  • select "Receive from API" if you want to send text from the MysterSmith app to Notarized (fake Notes app on spectator's phone)
  • API Auto Send: set to ZERO if you only want to send data when the phone is face down (or held against the chest), or set the number of seconds when you want to automatically send the text from Notarized to MysterSmith
  • you can select "Tap to Test API" to test if MysterSmith receives the data correctly

docs.title: Performance - send to MysterSmith
docs.text:
• you don't have to run Notarized on your phone (just make sure you've selected "Send to API")
  • in MysterSmith go to Settings - WEB-POLLING - WEB data sources
  • enable Notarized (and you can disable all other sources)
  • start WEB-polling
  • touch your prepared NFC card to the spectator's iPhone, and start the fake Notes app
  • the spectator can write something in the fake Notes app
  • after X seconds (based on your setting) the text will appear in MysterSmith (and displayed on your connected devices)

docs.title: Performance - receive from MysterSmith
docs.text:
• you don't have to run Notarized on your phone (just make sure you've selected "Receive from API")
  • touch your prepared NFC card to the spectator's iPhone, and start the fake Notes app
  • pretend to write a prediction (you can write anything)
  • put the spectator's iPhone face down
  • in MysterSmith you can connect an impression board, or use any other input method to get the info you want to transmit
  • when the text is added to the text buffer, Notarized will receive the info and paste it in the fake Notes app

docs.title: Using the API in the MysterSmith app
docs.text:
The easiest way to use the Dictionary API is the integrated support in the MysterSmith app.

First of all you will need to enter/get the word somehow - this can be achieved by a handful of methods:

  • manual text entry (by an assistant)
  • text recognition (from the Doodle screen or impression boards)
  • swami input (thumb-writer)
  • polling from Inject
  • reading NFC cards
  • from another app via the custom URL scheme
  • from any 3rd party source via an API

Then you will need to trigger the "Dictionary API position" action (see the screenshot), using any of the available action triggers (PeekSmith button press, Atom remote button press, volume buttons, Apple Watch tap/swipe etc).

The app will then query the info from the webserver (internet connection needed), and display the results in a short/long version, depending on the type of the display. Please see the screenshots for a better understanding.

Explanation for the short version (the one you see on the PeekSmith Screen):

  • first row: page, column and line number (if you see an "e" before the column number, it means "extra column")
  • second row, first info (left): the number of the word, + means from top, - means from bottom
  • second row, second info (right): the vertical position of the word, abbreviated (see details below)
  • top! = at the top
  • top+ = around the top
  • mid! = at the middle
  • bot- = around the bottom
  • bot! = at the bottom
  • estimated vertical positions can be: 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4

Some examples explained:

15 e3 11 +11   1/3

Page 15, extra column 3, line 11 11th word from the top, around the 1/3 of the column

206 2 1 +1   top!

Page 206, column 2, line 1 1st word from the top, exactly at the top

241 2 45 -4   3/4

Page 241, column 2, line 45 4th word from the bottom, around the 3/4 of the page

docs.title: Using the API with 3rd party apps
docs.text:
You can also use the "Dictionary API" with any 3rd party app or service, by accessing the WEB API directly. You will need two things for this: enable 3rd party access in the MysterSmith app (it will be active for 1 hour), and use your secret token in the API query.

In the MysterSmith app go to SETTINGS - DICTIONARY API - and turn ON "Enable 3rs party apps (1 hour)". This will activate the 3rd party access of the API URLs for 1 hour. If you turn the toggle OFF and then ON again, the 1 hour timeout will be reset.

Then locate and copy your API token, which can be found in the MysterSmith app: go to Settings - ACCOUNT SETTINGS - and tap "Show details". On the next page you will find the API token in the CREDENTIALS section. You can re-generate the token by tapping "Refresh", or copy the token to the clipboard by tapping the "API token" label with the clipboard icon.

Now you are ready to use the following API URLs from any 3rd party app or service.

docs.title: API URL for a brief text result:
docs.text:
https://bsmagic.app/api/dictionary/dictionary_get_text.php?token=XXXX&search=word

Replace "XXXX" with your token and "word" with the actual word you are looking for. The result will be a short summary of the location of the word in the dictionary:

docs.title: API URL for a more detailed JSON result:
docs.text:
https://bsmagic.app/api/dictionary/dictionary_get_json.php?token=XXXX&search=word

Replace "XXXX" with your token and "word" with the actual word you are looking for. The result will be a detailed info in JSON format about the location of the word in the dictionary:

Explanation of the JSON fields:

success: 0=error or 1=OK word: the word you were looking for page, column, line: the location of the word extra: 0=regular word with explanation, 1=word without explanation in the extra columns wordcount: the number of the word in the column (from top) wordcount_txt: detailed info about the number of the word verticalpos: short info about the vertical position of the word verticalpos_txt: detailed info about the vertical position of the word

If the success field returns a 0 value, there will be also an error message included for a better understanding.

docs.title: Try before you buy
docs.text:
You can try offline recognition before you purchase the add-on (or a subscription). Just enable the offline mode in TEXT RECOGNITION settings, and write something on the Doodle screen (or on a connected impression board). The recognized text will be displayed in the popup message, but the app won't save it in the text buffer for further processing. It means you can't display the recognized text on an external device, and you can't send it to other apps or services.

This way you can experiment how the offline recognition works in your own language, and if you're satisfied with the result, you can purchase the add-on (or a subscription), and process the recognized text in any way possible.

docs.text:
If you have already purchased the Offline text recognition add-on (or a subscription), you can not only display the recognition result, but you can process it many ways, just like you can do with regular text recognition. You can display the recognized text on an external display device, create time predictions, ESP drawings, magic squares etc. using the smart functions of the MysterSmith app.

You can even use the offline recognition as a backup method in case your internet connection drops out, or the regular recognition engine (Google or A.I.) returns no result.

The offline recognition engine doesn't use any credits, and no other payment is needed from your side (besides purchasing the add-on or a MysterSmith subscription of course).

  • If you cancel your subscription after 1 year of continuous subscription, you can turn 50% of the total paid fee into credits.
  • If you cancel your subscription after 1.5 years of continuous subscription, you can turn 75% of the total paid fee into credits.
  • If you cancel your subscription after 2 years of continuous subscription, you can turn 100% of the total paid fee into credits.
  • If I ever decide to terminate the subscription model, you can turn 100% of the total paid fee of your currently active, continuous subscription into credits.

You can use these credits to purchase any add-ons and/or apps that were included in your subscription, but you don't own yet, at the actual retail price. The time limit for using your credits will match the duration of your continuous subscription.

Your credits can be only used for purchasing add-ons and apps for your own account.

docs.title: Using A.I. recognition (OpenAI or Gemini)
docs.text: In MysterSmith you can use A.I. based text and drawing recognition, which is using either GPT by OpenAI, or Gemini by Google. To use these A.I. based recognition engines, you don't need to buy any text recognition credits from me, but you'll have to create your own OpenAI or Gemini API key.

docs.title: Obtaining your OpenAI API key
docs.text:
To be able to use GPT-based A.I. text recognition (also drawing recognition and analysis), you will need to get an OpenaAI API key, and top up your balance (performing one routine will cost you only around 0.01-0.02 USD).

Follow these steps to get your OpenAI API key, to use in the MysterSmith app:

  • create an OpenAI account: https://platform.openai.com/signup
  • go to your billing overview: https://platform.openai.com/account/billing/overview
  • add your payment details
  • top up your API balance (with at least 10 USD)
  • create an API key: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

IMPORTANT: copy your API key as soon as you create it, you won't be able to view/copy it later!!! * in the MysterSmith app go to Settings, and scroll down to the API + A.I. ACCESS ADD-ON  section * paste your API key to "Your OpenAI API key" * select your language at "A.I. language" * in TEXT RECOGNITION settings select A.I. (GPT-4o) as the recognition engine

docs.title: How to create your Gemini API key
docs.text:
You can also use A.I. text and drawing recognition provided by Google Gemini, which can be used FREE of charge (up to a specified limit).

Here are the steps to create your Gemini API key, and to use it in MysterSmith:

  • visit the Google A.I. Studio: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
  • accept the Terms of Service
  • select API keys - "Create API key"
  • choose an existing project, or select "Create API key in new project"
  • your API key wil be displayed, copy it to the clipboard
  • make sure you have a username and PIN set up in in MysterSmith (Account Settings - Show details)
  • in MysterSmith go to API + A.I. Access settings
  • enter your Gemini API key
  • in Text Recognition settings select a Gemini model (2.5 Pro or Flash)
  • set "Automatic text recognition" to 3 sec, and enable "Show recognized text"
  • go to the Perform page and start the Doodle screen
  • write anything on the screen (or use an impression board)
  • the recognized text will pop up at the bottom of the screen
  • you can also try automatically performing an action after text recognition (see the screenshots and photos below)

In Google A.I. Studio you can view the usage (and optional billing) reports. Using Gemini A.I. recognition is FREE up to 5/10 recognitions a minute (Pro / Flash), and 100/250 recognitions a day.

docs.title: The basic CLOCK SWIPE method
docs.text:
First of all, this swipe method is the idea of Paul Longhurst, who was kind enough to let me implement it into TimeSmith.

The idea of the clock swipe method is that you can input any number with exactly 2 swipes. For this you'll have to imagine a clock face with numbers 1 to 12 (where number 12 can also represent number 0). You will have to swipe the screen of your phone (or push the buttons of your 4-button BT remote) to any of these 4 directions: UP, DOWN, LEFT or RIGHT.

Here is a video where I'm explaining how to swipe to any of the 12 numbers:

docs.title: The first swipe
docs.text:
• if the first swipe is UP, you go to number 0/12
  • if the first swipe is RIGHT, you go to number 3
  • if the first swipe is DOWN, you go to number 6
  • if the first swipe is LEFT, you go to number 9

docs.title: The second swipe
docs.text:
• if the first swipe was UP, and your second swipe is UP again, then you stay on number 0/12
  • if the first swipe was UP, and your second swipe is RIGHT, then you go to number 1

  • if the first swipe was UP, and your second swipe is LEFT, then you go to number 11

  • if the first swipe was RIGHT, and your second swipe is RIGHT again, then you stay on number 3

  • if the first swipe was RIGHT, and your second swipe is UP, then you go to number 2

  • if the first swipe was RIGHT, and your second swipe is DOWN, then you go to number 4

  • if the first swipe was DOWN, and your second swipe is DOWN again, then you stay on number 6

  • if the first swipe was DOWN, and your second swipe is RIGHT, then you go to number 5

  • if the first swipe was DOWN, and your second swipe is LEFT, then you go to number 7

  • if the first swipe was LEFT, and your second swipe is LEFT again, then you stay on number 9

  • if the first swipe was LEFT, and your second swipe is UP, then you go to number 10
  • if the first swipe was LEFT, and your second swipe is DOWN, then you go to number 8

docs.title: What does text recognition do?
docs.text: By default the MysterSmith app is using the handwriting recognition service by Google Vision. You can send handwritings from the Doodle screen, from the WEB-doodle or from supported impression boards, and you will receive the recognized text. This text can be displayed on your PeekSmith device, supported smartwatches and all other displays (you'll need the External Displays add-on for this to work).

docs.title: A better alternative to Google Vision: A.I. recognition
docs.text:
You can also use A.I. based text recognition, which is using either GPT by OpenAI, or Gemini by Google. To use these A.I. based recognition engines, you don't need to buy any text recognition credits from me, but you'll have to create your own OpenAI or Gemini API key.

For GPT based recognition you will have to top up your OpenAI account with at least 10 USD (paid directly to OpenAI), while using Gemini is FREE (up to a certain limit). For more information please visit this page:

mystersmith.info/ai-recognition

docs.title: The prerequisites of using text recognition
docs.text:
To use the text recognition feature, you must have your Username and PIN set up first. If you haven't set your Username and PIN yet, go to USER SETTINGS and tap the empty Username field. There you can add any username (that is not already taken) and set any 4-6 digit number as your PIN.

You will also have to turn ON the "Enable text recognition" option in the TEXT RECOGNITION section.

docs.title: Recognition credits (for Google Vision engine only)
docs.text:
If you use Google as the recognition engine, the recognition of one page (no matter how many text it contains) uses 1 recognition credit. Every user gets 250 credits for free when they create their user account. If you're running out of credits, you can buy recognition credits from me. You can check your credit balance in the TEXT RECOGNITION section ("Recognition credits left").

Click here to buy text recognition credits

docs.text:
If you already have the "API + A.I. access" add-on, you can enter your own OpenAI API key or Gemini API key to be able to use A.I. based features, like text recognition, image analysis and more.

IMPORTANT: If you go with this option, you will not use Google Vision as the recognition engine, and you won't need to buy any recognition credits from me.

For details and instructions please visit this page: A.I. text recognition

docs.title: Triggering text recognition
docs.text:
The recognition should be triggered, either automatically or by invoking an action.

To use the automatic recognition, go to the TEXT RECOGNITION section and set "Automatic recognition" to 3 seconds or more (depnding on your routine). After writing something, recognition wil trigger when you don't write anything for X seconds.

There are also some text recognition actions which can be assigned to triggers like PeekSmith buttons, Atom remote buttons, Apple Watch screen taps or swipes, WearOS watch screen taps, volume button presses etc. Some of these triggers can be found in the ACTION CONTROL section of the settings page, while some triggers can be found somewhere else (like on a device config page).

docs.title: Text recognition settings explained
docs.text:
Recognition engine: select the preferred recognition engine (Google Vision, GPT by OpenAI, Gemini by Google, or even Offline mode)

Recognition method: select the option you need for your routine. You can recognize text/numbers, playing cards, ESP cards, timestamps, drawings etc.

Display profress message: enable this to receive a notification when text recognition is in progress

Transform Chinese/Hebrew text: enable this fi you use Chinese/Hebrew text recognition, and you want to convert the recognized text using the letters of the English alphabet

Correct spelling/names: if you enable this, the A.I. will try to correct your misspellings any typos automatically

Short card names: recognized playing cards will be converted to a format like AH, 5D, 10C, KS etc.

Automatic recognition: you can set a timer that will trigger recognition automatically X seconds after the user stopped writing on the Doodle screen or impression board. For example if you set this to 5 seconds, and the user writes a word, text recognition will automatically happen 5 seconds after they stop writing.

Show recognized text (pop-up): enable this to see the recognized text either in a pop-up message, or as a large text on the BLACK SCREEN

Clear canvas for next drawing: if you enable this, then you can perform multiple text recognitions using the same impression board (or Doodle screen), without the need to manually clear the previous writing. If you write a new word after a successful text recognition, the doodle screen will be cleared automatically as soon as you start writing

Action after recognition: if you want something to happen automatically after a successful text recognition, set this option to 1 or more seconds

Trigger action: select what should happen automatically after a text recognition

Rubik's cube colors: enable this option if you want to recognize colors on a drawing of a Rubik's cube face

CubeSmith integration: enable this option if you want to automatically awitch to CubeSmith after recognizing the colors on a cube face drawing

Numbers only: turn this option ON if you only want to recognize numbers (like for a LOTTO routine or Pi Revelations)

Pi Revelations (4 digits): if you enable this option, the app will show you the Pi Revelations numbers after recognizing a 4 digit number

LOTTO routine: enable this if you wnat to recognize LOTTO numbers

Numbers in ascending order: if you enable this, the LOTTO numbers will be arranged in ascending order

Last number as JOKER: enable this if the last number written should be a JOKER / EXTRA number (won't be included in the ascending order)

1-digit numbers with zeros: turn 1 digit numbers to 01, 05, 07 etc. format

Remove commas between numbers: return the recognized LOTTO numbers separated by SPACES instead of commas
